title: The Star Money
summary: A kind girl with no money gives her clothes away and meets falling stars.
coverScene: A poor young girl stands in a quiet field at night, looking up as bright stars fall down toward her.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, there was a very poor little girl whose father and mother had both died.
She had nothing left in the world except one small room and the clothes upon her back.
Because she was so nice, she gave away every piece of bread which she had to other people.
She also gave away every bit of money which she possessed to anyone who asked her.
She did this because her heart was full of love and care for every human being.
She wanted to make sure that no person suffered while she had something to share.
Her life was hard, but she always found a way to help those who needed support.
She never kept anything for herself, believing that sharing was the best thing to do.
Every single day, she walked around the town and looked for individuals in difficult situations.
Whenever she saw someone who lacked food, she gave them whatever she had in her hands.
Her gentle nature made her well known among the local residents who respected her greatly.
Although she had very little, her giving spirit was larger than any house in the city.
She believed that being good to others mattered more than having wealth or possessions.
Her parents had taught her to be nice before they passed away from this life.
She remembered their words every time she made a decision to help a stranger.
Day after day, she continued this wonderful habit without showing any sign of sadness.
She felt happy whenever she brought a smile to the face of a tired person.
Nothing could stop her from doing good acts because her spirit was strong and pure.
She lived through many difficult months, yet her warm care remained constant and true.
People often wondered how she managed to survive with such a giving and open heart.
One day, the good child walked out into a field alone, because she had no home left.
An old man met her on the road and asked her for something to eat.
She gave him her last bit of food without any pause, wishing that she could help him more.
The old man thanked her with a warm smile and walked away into the distance.
She stood there for a moment and felt glad that the old man had food now.
Soon after that, she met a little boy who was crying because his head was cold.
She took off her coat and gave it to him, so that he would feel warm.
The boy put on the coat and stopped crying immediately as the cold wind left him.
She smiled at the child and watched him run off to play with his friends.
A little further down the path, another child asked for her dress.
Without thinking twice, she gave that away too and remained with very few clothes.
She did not care about the cold wind that began to blow across the open field.
Her mind was at peace because she had made three children feel safe and happy.
She continued walking down the long road as the afternoon turned into evening.
The sun went down behind the hills, and the shadows grew longer across the ground.
She knew that she would have to spend the night outside under the open sky.
She was not afraid of the dark because she had done nothing wrong in her life.
Her gentle actions gave her the strength to keep moving forward despite everything.
She trusted that something good would happen to her before the morning came.
Her belief in doing good kept her going when the path became hard to see.
When night came, she found herself in a dark forest with no clothes and no food left.
Suddenly, stars began to fall down from the sky above her like bright silver money.
She looked up and saw that the stars were turning into fine new clothes.
The clothes landed softly around her on the dark ground of the quiet forest.
The happy girl quickly gathered up the wonderful gifts which had been sent from above.
She put on the finest clothes and became a rich person who could help everyone.
From that day forward, she lived a good life and was never poor again.
She used her new wealth to build a large house where poor people could stay.
Many individuals came to her door, and she welcomed every single one of them inside.
She provided them with warm food, clean clothes, and a safe place to sleep.
Her name became famous throughout the country as a symbol of true love.
Children and adults together visited her home to share their stories and seek advice.
She listened to everyone with calm strength and gave them the support they required.
Her heart remained just as nice as it had been when she owned nothing.
She never forgot the hard days when she walked the roads without a coat.
Instead, those memories made her even more giving toward people in need.
Years passed by, but her reputation for doing good never faded away.
When she finally reached old age, she looked back at her life with total satisfaction.
She knew that her choices had made the world a much better place for everyone.
Her story was told from generation to generation as a wonderful example of love.

sentences.text: In a world shadowed by grief and quiet destitution, there lived a young orphan girl whose parents had departed this life, leaving her with nothing save for one barren chamber and the simple garments upon her back.
Bereft of worldly goods, she possessed an abundance of spirit, her heart overflowing with a boundless capacity for empathy towards every living soul.
It was her firm conviction that no human being should endure suffering while she retained even the smallest fragment to share.
Whenever she walked through the cobbled streets of the town, her eyes scanned the shadows for those weighed down by misfortune.
She routinely surrendered the very crust of bread from her pocket and every copper coin she owned to anyone who asked.
Her gentle disposition soon earned her the deep respect of the local residents, who watched in quiet wonder as she moved among them.
Though her own life was marked by bitter hardship, her altruism remained steadfast, stretching wider than the wealthiest estate in the city.
She believed implicitly that moral integrity and kindness outweighed any accumulation of gold or material treasures.
Her departed parents had instilled these virtues deeply within her soul before they passed away from this earthly existence.
Whenever she faced a difficult choice, she recalled their parting words and chose the path of compassion.
Day after day, she maintained this remarkable routine without a single murmur of discontent or a trace of sorrow.
A profound joy invariably bloomed within her chest whenever she coaxed even a fleeting smile onto the face of a weary laborer.
Nothing could deter her from performing acts of quiet grace, for her internal resolve was as pure as it was unyielding.
She endured months of biting cold and gnawing hunger, yet her warmth toward others never once flickered.
Neighbors often marveled at how she managed to survive day by day with a spirit so utterly unguarded and open.
Eventually, the inevitable arrived, and she was forced to abandon her last shelter, stepping out alone into an open field.
The sky above was heavy with grey clouds, and a bitter wind swept across the empty landscape as she began her solitary journey.
It was along this desolate road that she encountered an elderly man whose posture was bent heavily beneath the weight of years.
He approached her with trembling hands and asked if she might spare a morsel of food to quiet his rumbling stomach.
Without a moment of hesitation, she handed him her very last piece of bread, wishing with all her soul that she had more to offer.
The old man accepted the gift with a tender smile, offering his gratitude before turning to walk away into the gathering mist.
She stood motionless on the path for a long moment, feeling a quiet surge of gladness that the traveler's immediate hunger was now eased.
Scarcely had she resumed walking when she encountered a small boy weeping bitterly beside a stone wall.
He cried out that his head and shoulders were freezing in the sharp wind, and that he had no protection against the frost.
Without a second thought, she slipped her woolen coat from her shoulders and wrapped it snugly around the shivering child.
The moment the heavy fabric settled over him, the boy stopped crying, the biting chill banished from his small frame.
She offered him a reassuring smile and watched as he scrambled away with a newfound energy to join his companions in the distance.
Continuing down the winding path, she had walked only a little further when another child timidly asked for her dress.
Though the afternoon air was turning rapidly to ice, she did not hesitate to part with the garment, leaving herself clad in almost nothing.
She cared little for the wind that now cut straight through her remaining layers, her mind anchored in a deep, serene peace.
She had successfully warmed three vulnerable children, and that knowledge served as an invisible cloak against the elements.
Onward she walked as the autumn afternoon slowly dissolved into a bruised and darkening evening.
The sun dipped below the distant hills, stretching long, skeletal shadows across the frosted grass of the open fields.
She knew with absolute certainty that she would be forced to spend the coming night shivering beneath the open sky.
Yet fear found no purchase in her heart, for she had lived honorably and caused harm to no living creature.
Her virtuous actions provided her with an inner fortitude that sustained her steps when the horizon vanished entirely from view.
She trusted implicitly that some unseen grace would intervene before the cold light of dawn broke across the world.
When complete darkness finally swallowed the landscape, she found herself deep within the silent shadows of a vast forest.
She possessed neither food nor proper clothing, utterly exposed to the chill of the midnight woods.
Suddenly, a wondrous phenomenon occurred above her as the velvet ceiling of the night sky seemed to fracture.
Bright stars began to detach themselves from the firmament, tumbling downward through the branches like coins of pure silver.
As she looked upward in breathless wonder, she realized those falling lights were transforming into garments of the finest silk and wool.
The rich clothes drifted downward through the quiet air, landing softly upon the dark, mossy earth around her feet.
With trembling hands, the astonished girl gathered the celestial gifts and dressed herself in attire fit for a queen.
Transformed in an instant, she was no longer a destitute outcast, but a person of abundant means who could finally heal the world around her.
From that remarkable night onward, she lived a life of great influence, ensuring that poverty never touched her threshold again.
She utilized her newfound wealth to construct a sprawling manor where the homeless and the hungry could always find sanctuary.
Countless travelers came to her heavy oak doors, and she welcomed every single soul inside with genuine hospitality.
She provided them with steaming bowls of broth, sturdy garments, and secure beds to chase away the nightmares of the road.
Her name quickly echoed across the borders of the country, becoming universally recognized as a living symbol of profound charity.
People of all stations traveled great distances to visit her home, seeking counsel or simply wishing to share their personal griefs.
She listened to every petitioner with unwavering patience and calm wisdom, offering whatever material or spiritual support was required.
Despite her great riches, her heart remained as humble and tender as it had been when she owned nothing at all.
She never once forgot the bitter wind biting through her thin dress during those long years on the open road.
Instead, those difficult memories only served to deepen her generosity toward the unfortunate who knocked at her door.
Decades slipped away like water through cupped hands, yet her legendary reputation for goodness never dimmed with the passing years.
When she finally reached old age, she surveyed her long life with a profound sense of peace and absolute fulfillment.
She understood that her courageous choices had permanently altered the landscape of human suffering for the better.
Long after she departed this world, her remarkable journey was recounted by parents to their children around winter hearths.
It remained forever etched in human memory as the ultimate testament to the quiet, transformative power of unconditional love.
